findings.place: 4.11 stripRegions (line 648) and writePublicSet step (5) (line 650); section 5 E14 (line 729); section 7, second item (lines 761–762); section 10 PB-6 (lines 915–922: «a planted unclosed region … — the first two make writePublicSet throw»); section 13
findings.what: The cut pairs an opening marker with the nearest following end marker of its kind, and the guard of step (5) looks only for a marker left in the output. An opening marker that is not closed before another region of its kind begins — a nested opening marker, or a region whose own end marker is missing — is therefore paired with the next region's end marker: everything between is cut, every marker is gone, no guard fires, and the build ends 0. Measured on my fresh clone of the build tag with the sketch's public-set.js (<scratch>/v1d/t5; my trials ps-planted.mjs and ps-nested.mjs): an unclosed «<!-- sai:order -->» planted before the footer's own order region → writePublicSet does not throw, no marker is left, and the footer lost its home link «Главная»; a nested opening marker → the same; an unclosed marker after the last region and a stray end marker do throw («index.html: a region the build cannot strip»). On the designer's realistic pages (f2pages, copied) with only block D's end marker dropped: negative checks 0, PB-2's strict comparison 0 (its oracle uses the same nearest-end rule), PP-7 red (#ai-disclosure gone) and PB-6's content rule red (5 lines). So production stays guarded by the tests of npm run check (PB-6's source rule, its content rule, PP-7), but E14's named behaviour («exit 1») and section 7's «nothing reaches the platform's output unchecked» are false for this class of input, and PB-6's planted unclosed region «makes writePublicSet throw» only where no later region of its kind follows: planted in the natural place on index.html (block D left open, the footer region after it) it does not throw, so the test as written is red against code built exactly by 4.11, and the developer and TEST-DESIGNER would have to choose.
findings.needed: Make the build refuse in the same call what it cannot cut correctly (a change of approach, not another pattern): before any cut, writePublicSet reads the markers of each .html file as a sequence and throws, naming the file, on an opening marker while one of its kind is open, an end marker with none open, or an opening marker never closed — the pairing of the input, not only the output; E14 and section 7 then hold as written. PB-6 names its planted shapes and their positions — a region left open before a later region of its kind (index.html with block D's end marker dropped), a nested opening marker, a stray end marker — each making writePublicSet throw; section 13 gains the mutant «the cut with no pairing check», killed by the first plant.
